completionPackage.summary: Inventoried the person → user → role → scope authority chain across web/, docs/platform/, and supabase/migrations/. Wrote a 443-line file-grounded markdown inventory. Headline structural finding: the person→user leg does not exist — `persons` carries no link to `auth.users`, so principal and subject are disjoint graphs joined only by query-time scope filtering. Executed web/scripts/auditAuthorityPaths.mjs (deferred unrun by the prior phase) and established that its tier-3 census of 507/539 routes is a measurement artifact: 490 routes are credited to modules that resolve permissionKeys without consulting them. Ground-truth enforcement is 17 routes via 8 modules. Enumerated 9 contradictions (C1-C9) and 6 gaps (G1-G6), each cited path:line, including a canonical governance doc whose stated rule, claimed foreign key, and expanded-reference pointer are all contradicted by the codebase. No source files were modified.

tests.results: No test suite applies to a documentation deliverable. web/scripts/auditAuthorityPaths.mjs was executed read-only as evidence for C1; its output is quoted verbatim in §3.

validation.evidence_ref: Every claim cites path:line against files read in this worktree. Primary sources: web/lib/admin/resolveAdminAccessCore.ts, getAdminAccessContext.ts, adminRouteGate.ts, accessScope.ts, canManageUsersAndRoles.ts, permissionGrid.ts, middleware.ts, operatorSessionGate.ts; web/app/api/admin/rbac/grants/route.ts, users/[userId]/role/route.ts, configuration/programs/route.ts, persons|customers|global-search/route.ts; supabase/migrations/20260329165048_remote_schema.sql, 20260504103000, 20260505120000, 20260505120100, 20260505153000, 20260505164000, 20260523150000, 20260718140000; docs/platform/governance/roles-and-permissions.md, api-contracts.md, glossary.md. §8 gives runnable reproduce commands for every count.

§3 enumerates contradictions C1-C9; §4 enumerates gaps G1-G6; §5 tabulates enforced-vs-configured across 13 authority concepts; §6 states what this phase confirms and corrects in the prior inventory (docs/platform/planning/access-identity-v2/inventory.md), including two corrections to it; §7 states 7 explicit limits.

risks: G1 (handle_new_user defaults every new auth user to `ops`) is unverified against the live database — no CREATE TRIGGER on auth.users exists in migrations or baselines, but absence in version control is not absence in the deployed DB. Verification query supplied in §7.3.

G2 (routes relying on getAdminAccessContextCached alone, which never checks portalEligible) is a latent hazard, not a confirmed defect. The set-difference over 88 route files was not computed — the required shell forms were declined by the session command policy; three sensitive routes were sampled by hand and all correctly pair it with a portal gate. Exact command in §8.
Token strength for the 28 tier-0 routes, webhook signature verification, and RLS policy content were not audited — stated as limits, not silently omitted.
C5 (unsavable Workflows grid row) is derived statically from the seed migrations and the grants-API validation path; it was not reproduced in a browser.
followUp: Product decision required before a canonical model can be specified: is a `persons` row ever a principal? (§9 Q1)
Portal admission model: derive portalEligible from a granted permission, or introduce a portal-access permission custom roles can hold (§9 Q2) — resolves C6 and C7 together.
Make PERMISSION_GRID_ROWS a projection of the enforced key set rather than an independent list (§9 Q3) — makes C5 impossible by construction and turns C4 into a visible gap.
web/scripts/auditAuthorityPaths.mjs needs a resolves-vs-consults distinction before its census is quotable; left unmodified as out of scope for this deliverable.
G3 needs a product ruling: a `settings.users_roles` holder can currently set any user's role, including their own, to `admin` — no ceiling and no self-assignment guard.
